completeCurrentRecord.name: Anatomy Lore

sourceObject.name: Anatomy Lore
sourceObject.description: You have studied the weak joints, organs, and pressure points of giants, ogres, and other colossal foes common to Aethel's wilds. Prestige lineage: Giant Killer. completed from the existing development record.)
sourceObject.prerequisite: Intelligence 13+, proficiency in Knowledge (Monstrous Humanoids) or Survival
sourceObject.effect: As a bonus action, you can identify one weak point on a Large or larger creature you can see. Your next attack against that creature deals +50% damage if it hits, or you gain advantage on the attack if the target is Huge or larger. Once per short rest, when you hit a colossal foe with this advantage, you may force it to succeed on a Strength save or have its speed halved until the end of your next turn.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: As a Bonus Action, mark one actually visible Large-or-larger creature with a perceivable physical weak point and legal line of effect. NEW: maximum range 60 feet; keep at most one such mark, replacing the old one without refund. At marking choose damage mode, or advantage mode if the target is Huge or larger. The mark lasts until the end of your next original regular turn, using the current virtual-marker rules if initiative changes. It is consumed by your next actual attack roll against that target, hit or miss; attacks against others neither consume it nor receive its benefit. Damage mode adds half, rounded down, of that attack's own rolled weapon/natural/unarmed damage dice plus its ordinary ability modifier after its actual critical-dice adjustment, minimum zero. Do not include spell damage, separate riders, copied damage, added Smite/sneak dice or another percentage enhancement in this proposal's base. Add this extra amount as the attack's native damage type before target defenses, once. Advantage mode gives advantage to that next attack; ordinary cancellation still applies. Once per completed short rest, after an actual hit from advantage mode against a Huge-or-larger marked target, you may spend the use to force a Strength save against DC 8 + PB + INT modifier. On failure halve that target's current applicable movement Speeds until the end of your next original regular turn; do not stack same-family halves. NEW: the rider can qualify when the feat's advantage was canceled, because the selected paid mode still applied. The creature must possess relevant anatomy; no taxonomy or immunity is rewritten. The same attack cannot claim this proposed percentage enhancement and another percentage enhancement on the same base: select one, retaining other independently legal flat/dice riders.
sourceDirection.submittedNewChoices: Range, mark deadline/consumption, actual anatomical gate, damage base and ordering, mode lock, DC, Huge meaning of colossal, canceled-advantage bridge and percentage-family rule. Must confer with Precision Strike/Giant Slayer and full class damage scope.
submittedWorkedCases: A legal marked damage-mode weapon hit has 2d6 totaling 7 plus STR 3: its base is 10 and the rider adds 5 before defenses. An independent 1d6 damage rider is resolved normally but is not included in that half-base.

Against a Huge foe, choose advantage mode. If disadvantage cancels it and the ordinary roll still hits, the proposed slow rider may spend its short-rest use; a successful Strength save prevents the slow but does not refund that use.
sourceDirection.decision: Preserve source next-attack scope including spell attacks, remove invented weapon-only exclusion and percentage monopoly; retain real anatomy, one mark, Huge choice and the paid slow.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure:
Keep spellcasting ability and total character level3. NEW finite recovery interpretation: once per beneficial Long Rest, after your own genuine attack resolves with a kept natural20, recover up to2RP into an existing actual pool, capped by missing RP and an eligible previously paid rank1 spell cost from this same rest epoch. Choose one committed rank1 cast receipt that actually spent RP before this attack and still has at least1unrecovered paid RP. Refund at most the lesser of2, its remaining paid amount and missing pool capacity; mark exactly that paid amount recovered so it cannot fund this feat again or a second refund of the same expense. A discounted1RP cast funds at most1; a free innate cast funds0. You may decline and keep the use; a declaration with no eligible paid receipt or no missing capacity is ineligible.

The qualifying attack may be a weapon or spell attack, including a genuine cantrip attack, but must be yours against a conscious, independently acting actual hostile opponent presenting a real encounter threat. NEW anti-farming exclusions: no object, self, willing training partner, compliant captive, your own controlled/summoned creature, copied/reflected roll or fabricated repeat of a natural20. A legitimate hostile opponent’s immunity does not erase its actual natural20 attack trigger; damage is not a printed requirement. An expanded critical on19, automatic hit, hypothetical die or replaced natural20 that was not kept does not qualify. Companions using your spell attack bonus are still different attackers. Resolve any triggering attack’s consequences first; recovery cannot retroactively pay an unaffordable cast or prevent that event’s death. No spell slot or “ranked recovery” pool is created.

Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, whether magical or nonmagical, and add 2 damage on each actual successful melee attack you own. sourceObject.name: Companion Training
sourceObject.description: Your beasts do not merely follow—they fight as extensions of your will across Aethel's wild tiers, answering whistle and gesture like soldiers who never learned fear. Prestige lineage: Beastmaster. completed from the existing development record.)

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Require the exact Animal Companion feat OR actual Animal Handling proficiency. Your genuinely bound/tamed Beast companions under your lawful current command gain+2 to their attack rolls and+2flat once per native attack damage roll, not per die/type or critical doubling. NEW no benefit to an ordinary allied Beast, non-Beast construct/undead/familiar, or a body you have no actual companion/control relation with. Original source-owner stats remain; add this feat layer once across overlapping trainers. For real tracking checks, if you are proficient in Survival, the companion uses its ownWIS plus your currentPB as the inherited proficiency contribution; expertise is not inherited, and a better real own contribution can replace it, not add twice. If you lack Survival proficiency, nothing is inherited. During your regular turn spend the sharedBAcommand within60ft to one companion that can hear you, selecting attack, Dash, Disengage or Help. At total level10+, the same command can name two audible owned companions taking that same action in their attached phases. This changes command recipient count only: one shared offensive companion action per owner numbered round remains. For attack, designate at most one to spend that offense; the other may move defensively and Dodge, not bank an attack. Two pure support actions can both resolve if legal. Command fails without refund if eligibility is lost; no extra independent turns/Reactions. When one of your actually commanded Beast companions reduces a meaningful hostile from positiveHP to0, you gain one advantage entitlement for your next attack against a creature within30ft of you before your next future regular end. NEW only an attack meeting30ft consumes it; a farther attack does not. Same-family reapplication refreshes one entitlement/deadline, never queues multiple. Death is not required, source floors/copy/no-reward restrictions apply.

A commanded Beast downs a hostile: the owner's next attack within30ft gains advantage before the deadline; no extra attack is granted.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: On a hit with a melee weapon attack, before rolling damage, select one held reachable object and forgo one actual base-weapon damage die to attempt disarming it. NEW remove one die before critical doubling; a critical1d8 weapon forgoes its entire doubled base2d8, retaining lawful flat damage and independent riders. Never pay with a rider die, a die already spent on another feat, or a fixed-damage expression. The target chooses STR or DEX save against DC8+PB+the actual attack ability modifier. Resolve remaining hit damage, then the save if the creature still holds the object. Failure drops it into an adjacent legal unoccupied space you choose, otherwise its own space. No extra damage to object, severed curse or bond; actual non-droppable bonds prevent dropping. An object wielded with two hands is still one object. No new once-turn cap: each separately paid qualifying hit can attempt, but the chosen die is spent even if immunity prevents the result.

submittedWorkedCases: A1d8 sword critical spends its one base die, leaving zero sword dice rather than one; STR modifier and a separately paid legal rider remain.
A target's bonded blade cannot drop. The attacker's declared damage die is still forgone; the bond is not broken.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Increase Constitution by 1, normally no higher than 20, and recompute the real derived modifier and maximum-HP records without healing. For each actual Hit Die legally spent and rolled to restore HP, NEW: set that die's pre-healing-modifier amount to the greatest of its ordinary die-plus-CON healing amount, twice the current signed CON modifier, and zero. Apply the minimum after the ordinary die-plus-CON calculation, separately per die, before ordinary healing bonuses, reductions, blockers and maximum/Critical caps. The resulting actual HP gain may be less than this raw minimum or zero. It creates no Hit Die, rest permission or automatic restoration of spent dice. Wounds reduce actual Hit Dice recovery under their existing rule, not this individual die's result. Do not floor the die face itself at twice CON or multiply a combined multi-die pool a second time.
sourceDirection.submittedNewChoices: Per-die floor after die-plus-CON, nonnegative bound and placement before ordinary healing pipeline.
submittedWorkedCases: CON modifier +3 with a Hit Die face of 1 normally gives 4; Durable makes the raw healing 6 before actual healing modifiers and caps.
CON modifier -1 with a die face of 1 gives zero under the proposed floor, not negative healing. A genuine no-HP-gain effect can still prevent a positive Durable result.
sourceDirection.decision: Adopt per-HitDie max(ordinarydie+CON,2CON,0) before healing pipeline; source CON+1 capacity is not healing, no new HitDice.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: When you actually cause a living dying creature to become Stable by a legal Medicine stabilization or a real healer's-kit use, offer that recipient 1 HP. Use the ordinary Action/DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) route or the ordinary Action/one-kit-use route; an independently owned feature may explicitly change that action cost. NEW: treat the 1 HP as a direct state-recovery grant following the completed stabilization, not ordinary rolled healing. Broad cannot-regain-HP restrictions and the living-target gate apply; it receives no ordinary healing bonuses. Record one Field-Surgeon-family entitlement per recipient's own completed-long-rest epoch, shared across all practitioners. Commit it on the eligible offer even when HP gain is blocked. The actual stabilization remains recorded; if recovery is blocked the creature stays Stable at 0 with its normal existing recovery deadline. If positive HP is gained, clear the obsolete Stable deadline normally. A separately owned Field Medic temp-HP offer still uses the genuine stabilization event, even if the recipient is now at 1 HP. Already Stable or dead creatures create no new trigger.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Acquire with actual Precision Strike OR total level8. Against actual Large-or-larger creatures, add floor20% of each own direct damage event's eligible native amount before defenses, using shared noncompounding percent arithmetic. This broad damage clause includes own actual spell and weapon components but not periodic/copy/reflection/transfer or companion-owned attacks. Once per SR after a melee attack hits a Huge-or-larger creature, before damage declare the cripple use; after damage halve all its current Speed modes through its next future regular end, retaining spent movement cost. NEW no additional save is invented; same feat family halves once and actual immunities/specific movement protections apply. When a Huge-or-larger enemy misses you with a melee attack, you may spend Reaction for a separate5ft movement-cost step, then, only if that creature is within your own actual melee weapon/natural/unarmed reach and line, deal1d6 direct damage of that legal attack profile's native physical type (bludgeoning for unarmed) without an attack roll. You may step0 if already in reach; normal terrain/opportunity attacks/Speed restrictions apply. If the step cannot bring it into your reach, do not start this Reaction. The original source wording about stepping into its reach does not let you strike from beyond your own reach. It then has disadvantage on its next attack against you before its next future regular end, consumed hit or miss. Direct reaction damage is not a hit/critical, cannot start attack/heal/resource chains, and receives no added Giant Slayer percent because it is this feat's derived reaction packet.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: After computing the current body's ordinary physical carrying capacity and inventory Load capacity from actual Strength and size, double both capacities. It does not double an item's weight, remove carried cargo, alter casualty Load, enlarge a mount's capacity or multiply an already modified result twice. You may wield a weapon made for a body one size category larger than your actual current body without a size-only handling penalty. Use that weapon's actual reviewed item profile, hands, reach, damage and properties; the feat itself adds no damage die, reach, proficiency, free hand or two-size permission. An oversized weapon without a complete source profile remains an item-authoring dependency rather than receiving improvised bigger statistics. Real anatomy and Strength requirements still apply.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: NEW full healing procedure: as an Action, spend one real healer's-kit charge to treat one adjacent legally reachable living creature. Choose ordinary stabilization only, or this feat's healing treatment. A full actual kit has ten charges, costs 5 gp and weighs 3 lb under the reviewed item rule; transfer or partial use never refills it. Healing treatment has one entitlement per recipient per that recipient's completed short or long rest, shared across all Healer practitioners. Commit that entitlement and the charge before resolution even if healing is later blocked. If the recipient is dying, first cause an actual dying-to-Stable transition using this paid kit use, then resolve ordinary healing of 2d4 plus the practitioner's signed Wisdom modifier, minimum zero before the normal healing pipeline. One charge funds both parts of this single treatment. If HP gain is blocked, the stabilization remains with its genuine recovery deadline; if positive HP returns, close that obsolete deadline normally. A recipient whose healing entitlement is spent may still receive ordinary kit stabilization for its real charge and Action, without more feat HP. Already Stable creatures can receive the once-per-rest healing but create no new stabilization trigger. This removes no Wounds, Injury, disease or death. Independently owned Field Medic/Field Surgeon triggers require their actual source/event and own limits, with no duplicated kit charge or invented second stabilization.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Add 2 once to the actual saving throw against a mental effect meeting the shared proposed finite predicate. This can apply to an INT, WIS, CHA, CON or other save if the actual effect qualifies; it is not a blanket ability-based bonus. The same source cannot add twice when one effect both causes fear and deals psychic damage. No bonus applies to an opposed skill check, death save, ordinary concentration maintenance or an effect granting no save. NEW stacking completion: this distinct feat bonus can combine with Resilient Mind's independently applicable +1 Wisdom-save rider, subject to any explicit overriding source restriction; class-technique bonuses first obey their own strongest-only family. Preserve actual natural-save rules and any printed failure margin. The feat supplies no immunity, automatic success, new save, changed belief or agency override.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: NEW gain3luck points, initially full and restored to3 only on a completedLR; no overcap or conversion. On your own attack, ability/skill/tool check or save, after the initial d20 die/dice are visible but before the outcome and consequences are declared, spend at most1point to roll one additionald20. Choose either to keep the original dice unchanged or to replace one original die with the new face; then apply the roll's original normal/advantage/disadvantage selection over its original one/two positions. The added die is not a third freely best-kept die under disadvantage. Actual natural face is the final kept face; no source allows inventing an automatic result. It may affect an opposed check or death save because those are your checks/saves; it cannot reroll an enemy, a damage die, a flat result or a no-roll automatic failure. NEW one Lucky intervention per underlying roll event even if another rule later rerolls it. Resolve Elven Accuracy on initial eligible dice first, then Lucky; Elven Accuracy cannot reroll the added Lucky die. Other mandatory whole-roll replacements preserve their own order and consume the same event entitlement.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Acquire with permanentDEX13 OR the exact Weapon Focus feat. Once per turn before one weapon attack roll choose one mode. Ordinary mode takes−2 on that roll and, on hit, adds floor50% of its eligible native weapon damage before percentages/defenses; actual critical dice are included before this computation. NEW alternative critical mode is available when the actual target is currently Restrained, Grappled, or carries your actual active Anatomy Lore identified-weak-point record. Spend the once-per-SR critical use on declaration; take no−2 and no+50% from this feat for this attack. If it hits, treat it as critical; a miss remains a miss and spends the use and turn allowance. Condition/mark eligibility is rechecked at resolution; losing it leaves an ordinary hit with the use spent. Actual critical immunity remains; no additional critical multiplier. Either mode is mutually exclusive with Power Attack's trade on this same attack. Anatomy Lore's own separately legal bonus can coexist under its precise native-damage scope, with percentages from the same base; the weak-point prerequisite does not grant that feat or let another owner's undisclosed read qualify. A grapple by another creature suffices because that alternative predicate has no ownership restriction.

CURRENT ADOPTED MENTAL-EFFECT PREDICATE (FS-05). A qualifying mental-effect save is the effect's own save to prevent or end Charmed, Frightened, possession, compelled actions/speech, or an explicitly described alteration of thoughts, memories, beliefs, emotions or perceived sensory reality; also include a save directly against psychic damage. A generic INT/WIS/CHA save, mundane physical hazard or ordinary social check does not qualify solely by ability or theme. Tag the actual effect and outcome before the roll. This is the finite source definition already adopted for Iron Will and Resilient Mind; it supplies no new roll, immunity or concentration permission.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: After you take the Attack Action on your own turn while actually wielding a usable shield, you may spend BA that turn to bash a creature within5ft. It deals1d4+STR bludgeoning, minimum0, with ordinary critical doubling. A buckler counts only if its actual profile allows a striking shield body; this feat does not conjure a free weapon or bypass the shield hand. NEW this includes actual melee weapon, natural and unarmed attacks, but does not replace a spell's designated casting ability or a special attack expressly locked to another stat. completeCurrentRule.title: Credentials, training snapshots and real study
completeCurrentRule.wording:
Use actual current credentials, one proficiency contribution and the feat's selected branch. Thievery is the bounded thieves'-tools/DEX acquisition bridge, not a new universal skill. Mechanical Disable Device means an actual Engineering or thieves'-tools disarm interface; it does not authorize magical disarming. Knowledge (Monstrous Humanoids) remains an existing valid legacy credential; proficient INT(Nature) for that bounded anatomy is the NEW alternative bridge, with printed Survival still valid. Culture Lore may be an actual bounded credential or the explicitly selected History specialization. Agility means the stated Dexterity option, not another ability. Spellcraft is not silently aliased to Arcana; an actual legacy credential receipt is required where it is printed as a prerequisite, unless another printed alternative qualifies. Half-elf, Half-orc, Dragonborn, Sorcerer and Warlock labels are not silently turned into present ancestry/class identities. Existing genuinely authorized legacy grants remain evidenced; no new builder option follows.

**Weapon prerequisite bridge.** Apply this bridge only to an actual printed feat prerequisite, subject to any more specific acquisition direction in that feat’s final procedure. Where a prerequisite names a weapon or weapon type, require actual proficiency with that named current weapon profile/type. A generic Melee or Melee Proficiency prerequisite requires actual proficiency with at least one current melee-weapon profile; Ranged or Ranged Proficiency requires actual proficiency with at least one current ranged-weapon profile. Use the weapon profile’s actual classification, not merely the attack’s melee or ranged delivery: throwing a melee-class weapon does not by itself satisfy Ranged acquisition, and making a ranged spell attack supplies no weapon proficiency. An otherwise generic martial-weapon proficiency prerequisite requires proficiency with at least one actual martial-weapon profile, not all martial weapons; an explicitly stricter per-feat prerequisite remains stricter. Two-Handed or 2H Weapon acquisition requires actual proficiency with a weapon whose current profile possesses the Two-Handed property; proficiency with a Versatile-only weapon held in two hands does not satisfy that gate. Record the qualifying proficiency grant and weapon profile/type in the acquisition snapshot. These are acquisition credentials: they neither supply an item or proficiency nor make an otherwise unproficient attack proficient. They do not impose a new requirement to use the acquisition-qualifying weapon for every later feat event. Actual use-time weapon, proficiency where expressly required, grip, body, range, ammunition, action and other predicates remain those of the exact feat and governing procedure. All other printed ability, level, prerequisite-feat, class-access and earned-opportunity requirements remain mandatory. Class, feat, ancestry and item grants with similar names otherwise remain separate permissions.
Casting-prerequisite snapshot bridge — FEAT327-ACQ-03. NEW acquisition completion. Apply this bridge only to an actual feat acquisition prerequisite or its expressly required acquisition selection, subject to a more specific acquisition rule in that feat’s final procedure. A casting prerequisite requires a source-qualified personal spellcasting entitlement already acquired by the character and still retained at the acquisition snapshot. Record the actual grant, exact spell identity and source version, casting route, relevant class/rank gates, and the repertoire or preparation evidence that makes that route available. Class-level capacity, an RP or RC pool, a spell merely appearing on a permitted list, ownership of a spellbook or scroll, item-enabled casting, an unacquired class feature, and the prospective benefit of the feat being acquired do not by themselves supply this entitlement.

Retained entitlement versus immediate casting legality. A retained personal grant does not lose its acquisition credential merely because its renewable charge is currently empty, RP is insufficient, components or a suitable casting hand/voice are unavailable, the character is unconscious, or an existing temporary prohibition or suppression prevents casting. Ignore those immediate-use impediments only when evaluating this casting credential. Do not refill a resource, restore components, lift a prohibition, perform a cast, or establish that the feat-selection transaction itself is otherwise lawful. Actual casting still requires every current action, component, body, target, range, payment, concentration, strain and source-specific condition. An expressly ongoing or currently-active prerequisite in a particular feat remains an ongoing or currently-active prerequisite.

Qualifying repertoire and preparation. For a known-spell route, require the exact spell actually learned or personally granted, with its applicable source gates satisfied. For an ordinary prepared route, require the spell actually prepared at the snapshot, an actually acquired always-prepared grant, or another already-established source exception that authorizes casting it without ordinary preparation. An unprepared spellbook entry and the ability to prepare or substitute it later are insufficient for that spell’s credential. A future study period, rest, substitution, level-up selection or other repertoire change cannot be anticipated. A ritual route qualifies when the character actually possesses its ritual-casting permission and the particular spell meets that permission’s exact book, tag, rank and other repertoire requirements; no ritual need already have been cast. Do not extend one spell’s ritual overlay to another spell. Loss of a required repertoire source follows the actual class procedure: Wizard’s surviving prepared matrices remain available under its spellbook-loss rule, while an unprepared lost-book entry is not made available by merely planning its reconstruction.

Generic and specific predicates. “Spellcasting ability,” “Actual personal spellcasting ability,” and “Ability to cast at least one spell” require at least one qualifying personal spell route under this bridge; a qualifying rank-0 spell is sufficient. “Ability to cast cantrips” requires a qualifying rank-0 route. A named-spell prerequisite requires the exact required spell identity and permitted source version, not a similarly named class technique or item effect. A school prerequisite requires an actual matching school on the qualifying route. A rank prerequisite uses the spell rank actually supplied by that route and the final normalized predicate’s existing exact-rank or minimum-rank comparison, not total character level, maximum possible class rank, available RP, damage, or a higher price paid for a lower-rank spell. Where one predicate combines identity, school, rank or route restrictions, one qualifying route must satisfy that complete predicate; do not combine different routes’ most favorable fields. Distinct alternatives retain their existing AND/OR structure.

Removal, replacement and expiry. Reevaluate the retained grant and repertoire for every new feat acquisition. An actually removed, expired or lawfully retrained-away grant cannot support a new acquisition unless another independently qualifying route exists. Replacing a prepared matrix removes that ordinary prepared route for later snapshots unless another valid route to the spell remains. Temporary suppression or renewable depletion is not removal. Exhausting a genuinely nonrenewable permission follows its actual source: if the permission terminates, it no longer supplies a retained route. Under FS-01, a previously acquired feat keeps its original acquisition snapshot; later prerequisite loss does not erase that historical acquisition or waive any of the feat’s actual ongoing operating conditions.

Unassigned schools and required school choices. Preserve each source spell’s actual school value, explicit null or absent field. An absent, null or unassigned school is not Universal, Enchantment, Evocation, a wildcard, or a school inferred from damage type or a grant’s name. A school-unassigned personal rank-0 grant can satisfy generic spellcasting and cantrip predicates, but cannot itself satisfy a school-specific predicate. Supplementary Spell Focus additionally requires its mandatory permanent selection of an actual school supported by at least one qualifying acquired spell route at that same snapshot. Satisfying its generic spellcasting prerequisite without a supported school choice is insufficient to complete its acquisition. Another genuine route may support that choice. Subsequent loss or suppression of the supporting route does not reselect the school or erase the original acquisition; later benefits still require actual eligible casts through that fixed school.

Authored-candidate evidence versus runtime selection. For authored-candidate qualification, use the exact complete controlling authored spell procedure and its actual source-access binding, supported by the applicable review and fulfillment chain. A preserved earlier blocked catalog snapshot does not override an explicitly reviewed, version-linked operational descendant merely because the original remains unchanged. A separate selectionEnabled:false or disabled runtime adapter does not by itself invalidate that authored evidence. Neither a favorable label nor the existence of a reviewed spell supplies the character’s personal grant or repertoire history. Genuinely unfinished, null, unsupported or operationally unavailable payloads remain unavailable as positive casting witnesses. Preserve original statuses and live selection flags; this acquisition bridge neither enables runtime selection nor promotes another card.

Snapshot and payment. Preserve the exact prerequisite text and record the qualifying grant, spell/source/mode, actual school-field state and rank, repertoire/preparation or ritual basis, applicable class gates, controlling authored-procedure reference, and acquisition time. Temporary use blocks may be recorded separately but are not treated as grant removal. Missing grant, preparation, source-version or required-school evidence leaves that predicate unestablished rather than assumed true. Check all other printed ability, level, ownership, credential and earned-opportunity requirements independently. The feat’s own prospective spell grant cannot bootstrap its prerequisite, and one paid opportunity cannot fund two acquisitions.

For the six exploration training entries, snapshot each named skill separately at acquisition: grant proficiency if absent; grant the explicitly printed replacing Expertise only if already proficient. An acquired proficiency does not become Expertise merely because proficiency is later acquired elsewhere. If a fixed grant lacks that branch, duplication yields no replacement skill or Expertise. Skill Expert and Prodigy's ordered explicit selections use their own rules. Study, tutoring, language learning, formula research, copying and crafting are different tasks; a bonus or time discount on one does not migrate to another. Apply the actual minimum phase, calendar, rest and physical requirements.

External-credential evidence — FEAT327-ACQ-04. NEW evidence-contract completion; the four existing feat procedures and their prerequisite alternatives are retained. For frenzied_rage, divine_favor, elemental_body and dragon_blood, evaluate a required external credential under ACQ04-EC1 against the same character, world and ordered acquisition snapshot, using the exact operative prerequisite and source version, linked credential or event evidence, and that world's established authority for recording that fact. A source file establishes wording, not that a particular character acquired a feature, worships a deity, experienced an event or possesses a lineage. A name, nonempty story label, unchecked Boolean, prospective feat benefit or unrelated class/ancestry/item grant supplies no credential. The supporting grant, worship state or exposure event must already qualify before acquisition; same-time events require an authoritative earlier sequence. Worship must be established at that snapshot; exposure is a qualifying prior event, not a requirement to remain exposed. Apply the branch-specific facts and required choices in ACQ04-EC1 without adding doctrine, an exposure threshold, an element-to-plane matching rule or a legacy alias. A conditional, opaque test-world fixture can establish only a CONDITIONAL_ONLY predicate result within that fixture. It supplies no actual campaign history, selectable option, class feature, cosmology approval or entitlement. Missing, unbound, mismatched or insufficient evidence leaves a predicate UNESTABLISHED; affirmative incompatible evidence is CONTRADICTED. Neither result satisfies a required AND node, although a separately satisfied printed OR alternative remains valid. An ESTABLISHED_FOR_SNAPSHOT result requires independently admitted actual-world evidence and is not supplied by this review. Preserve all original source fields, absence/null distinctions, acquisition history and current status/selection flags. All other permanent-ability, level, parent-feat, mandatory-choice and earned-opportunity predicates remain independently required; one paid opportunity cannot fund two acquisitions. Later use still requires the exact feat's ongoing predicates. This evidence policy does not reopen ACQ-03 or change its casting-snapshot rules.

NEW FEAT335-ACQUISITION-AUDIT-01 profile-classification bridge, limited to Weapon Focus and Weapon Mastery: a specific unarmed-strike profile is an eligible choice when it is supplied by an actual current operative source and actual acquired proficiency covers it. The source-listed ordinary Unarmed strike remains a Simple melee training entry even though it is an attack option rather than an inventory object. An actual Simple-weapons proficiency grant covering that entry, or an express unarmed-strike proficiency grant, supplies the required training. An actually acquired Monk unarmed rule changes that same unarmed attack's operative statistics; its die progression alone is not a new paid profile or a free reselection. An acquired Troll Claws trait, explicitly used to make unarmed strikes, is an eligible specific Claws profile when the actor also has that actual unarmed-strike training. Bind both the real trait/body and its covering training grant; Claws alone grants no proficiency. No separate external training credential is necessary when those current-source grants already establish it. Another genuine natural profile remains source-qualified: require its actual profile and covering proficiency, whether an explicit unarmed bridge or another actual grant; neither an umbrella label nor this ruling supplies all-natural-weapon proficiency. No item, anatomy, attack or combined Monk/Claws damage formula is granted. Weapon Focus retains its express ongoing operative-proficiency requirement. Weapon Mastery checks proficiency at acquisition and retains its own matching-profile and total-level-six use predicates, without a new ongoing-proficiency gate. Its nonrepeatability, broadest applicable critical range, natural-19-meets-AC and natural-20-automatic-hit rules are unchanged.

completeCurrentRule.title: Distinct feat bonuses and retained comparison families
completeCurrentRule.wording:
NEW joint convention: after eligibility, flat numeric bonuses from DISTINCT feat identities add unless an explicit shared comparison family says otherwise. One feat identity contributes once to the same event/statistic across duplicate representations, sources and owners. This replaces Extended Magic's blanket strongest-same-stat proposal and the conflicting individual statements/examples named in the correction register. It does not rewrite the eight reviewed feats or reviewed maximum-HP components.
Class techniques still perform their own strongest-class-bonus comparison; spells perform their reviewed same-stat comparison; item, attire, tool, facility, cover and item-enhancement contributions retain their own reviewed families. Then add the independently legal feat contribution. A feat-created weapon/armor enhancement explicitly put into an equipment family remains there, not also a feat bonus. Same named condition penalties retain their own comparison rather than becoming additive because a feat created them. Advantage/disadvantage still cancel normally; more sources of advantage do not outvote one disadvantage. Damage resistance of the same scope applies once; immunity retains priority; keep the greatest remaining temporary HP, not their sum. Expanded critical ranges use the broadest applicable range rather than adding chance points. Copies cannot exploit a new family name to duplicate a source. Actual unusual source overrides retain their explicitly narrower predicates.

completeCurrentRule.title: Native damage, percentages and hostile slows
completeCurrentRule.wording:
NEW percentage convention: each separately eligible percentage feat computes its own floored increment from the SAME native packet, after actual critical-dice adjustment and its ordinary native ability/flat formula but BEFORE external riders, other percentage increments, saves and defenses. Add the increments; never multiply them together or floor a combined percentage instead of the separate increments. A feat's exact eligible base remains controlling: Anatomy Lore and Precision Strike do not acquire a giant-slayer multiplier on unrelated spells, for example. Added external Smite/sneak/copy/retaliation/rider packets do not enter another feat's native base unless expressly named. Apply a shared-area roll's increment once to that shared roll, then each actual target's save/defenses. For a mixed native packet requiring division, compute the increment once, distribute proportional to nonnegative native typed amounts by largest remainder with original component order breaking ties, and preserve integer totals. Do not add the full increment to each type. Additional dice are added before actual critical doubling and save fractions; a maximized die is not an actually rolled face for rolled-face triggers.
KEEP hostile slow arbitration: evaluate each adverse Speed effect against the same pre-control Speed and take the lowest surviving result; do not add Slasher and Crippling Strike's two -10 penalties, or subtract -10 again after a stronger half-Speed. Distinct records retain their own deadlines and suppression. Root/physical restraint, missing movement modes, terrain costs, burden, systemic Strain and actual Wounds retain their proper independent stages. No movement already spent is refunded. Percent damage addition is not the rule for percentage work/cost/consumption reductions: those use their specifically declared strongest-factor family.

completeCurrentRule.title: Roll type, reroll window and targets
completeCurrentRule.wording:
KEEP attacks versus AC, binary saves, fixed-DC Core tasks with natural shifts, and opposed totals with unchanged-state ties lost by the initiator. A +10 attack margin is not a critical. Natural 1/20 on attacks retain their attack rules; saves do not acquire task shifts. A failed-save reroll replaces the whole original one- or two-d20 procedure with the same actual modifiers and advantage/disadvantage, before consequences, unless the exact feat instead replaces a named die position. Use the replacement even if worse; a source cannot reroll its own replacement. Lucky and Elven Accuracy keep their separately specified die-position rules. Costs and prior consequences are not rolled back.
KEEP the current class target convention: 'ally' includes the owner unless the source says OTHER, or real geometry/activity inherently requires a different creature. Do not count the same person twice in 'you and an ally', a team, a flanking pair or an assistance role. 'Enemy' requires an actual current opponent, not every creature in range; meaningful-hostility and anti-farm gates apply only where the source/this register binds resource or encounter rewards. Do not add an enemy or anatomy gate to an unrelated ordinary attack merely as a blanket convention. Source perception, actual reach/line of effect, body eligibility and willing/understood channels remain real.

CURRENT ADOPTED MENTAL-EFFECT PREDICATE (FS-05). A qualifying mental-effect save is the effect's own save to prevent or end Charmed, Frightened, possession, compelled actions/speech, or an explicitly described alteration of thoughts, memories, beliefs, emotions or perceived sensory reality; also include a save directly against psychic damage. Actual concentration maintenance is a separate save, not automatically a mental-effect save because psychic damage caused it. A generic INT/WIS/CHA save, mundane physical hazard or ordinary social check does not qualify solely by ability or theme. Tag the actual effect and outcome before the roll. This is the finite source definition already adopted for Iron Will and Resilient Mind; it supplies no new roll, immunity or concentration permission.

completeCurrentRule.title: One clock, deadlines, rests and initial uses
completeCurrentRule.wording:
Use EX58's single elapsed clock, eight-hour Watches, actual task minutes, two-active-work-Watch ceiling and scheduled Rest. A change of scene, gate, holder, location, initiative, class representation or calendar label does not reset a resource. SR/LR in these new procedures mean the actual beneficial completed owner rest, with one beneficial Long Rest per 24 elapsed hours and at most two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests. A qualifying long rest restores a short-rest allowance as already governed. Extra safe Rest paying Rest Debt alone provides no second resource recovery. Recipient-rest limits use the actual named recipient's rest epoch.
NEW initial acquisition completion: the newly acquired limited-use feat begins with its specified full finite allowance, unless it expressly starts empty (such as accumulated stacks/charges). Reacquisition/alias duplication cannot initialize it again. An increase in a PB-based maximum increases capacity only, not current unspent uses. Genuine maximum-HP/RP/RC, Hit Die, reserve and slot changes never heal or refill unrelated current values.
Use each explicit own-turn/any-turn/round predicate literally. A per-round allowance has one numbered global-round identity; extra turns do not refresh it. A default 'your turn' feat allowance uses the owner's regular interval unless its exact source direction expressly retains any actual turn. Newly completed missing durations use the next future original regular marker specified by the row, not the already-underway marker, retaining virtual/absolute deadlines across schedule changes. Outside initiative use the governed six-second phase without double ticks. A missed trigger is not queued for later. An early ending does not refund time or a use.

NEW FEAT335-CADENCE-CHECK-01 completion, limited to feat procedures governed by FS-06: an otherwise unqualified "once per turn" allowance is once for that feat owner during each genuine actual creature turn in which its exact trigger legally occurs, whether that turn belongs to the owner or another creature. A separately sourced and actually occurring extra turn has a distinct actual-turn identity and can supply a distinct opportunity for that unqualified allowance; this rule grants no extra turn. Another Action, Bonus Action, attack, Reaction, nested event, target or resumed segment of the same actual turn does not create another turn identity. Returning to or replaying an already recorded turn retains that turn's spent claim. Actual body, movement, attack, casting, payment, causal-root and recipient restrictions still govern independently.

This completion does not replace an expressly regular-turn allowance or FS-06's existing default owner-regular-interval allowance for "your turn". In particular, Savage Attacker retains its stated own/off-turn regular-turn allowances, and Eldritch Combat retains its expressly regular-creature-turn shared embedded-cast cap plus its owner-regular-interval ordinary-append cap. Overrun's per-creature challenge limit belongs to the actual turn containing its qualifying Dash and subsequent movement; another Dash in that same turn does not renew it. Quickened Thought keeps its expressly any-later-actual-turn release window and the shared one-free-stored-release-per-owner/numbered-round cap, not a new bank at each turn. Per-round, encounter, underlying-roll/cast, recipient-rest and source-defined duration/deadline histories are not reset by an extra turn. Outside initiative retain the governed six-second procedure without inventing a turn from each action or counting an initiative transition twice. Source-specific temporal restoration remains separately governed; this completion supplies no rewind or unsupported extra-turn adapter.

completeCurrentRule.title: Damage, current capacity, healing and causal budgets
completeCurrentRule.wording:
Keep the reviewed damage/prevention/temp-HP/HP/Wound/death order and exact immunity/resistance/interception windows. Numeric actual damage means actual normal HP lost plus actual temporary HP absorbed, excluding overkill, damage prevented and mere state assignments. That metric never defeats an explicit no-resource origin, no-trigger ward/temp-HP rule or other causal prohibition: only source-qualified events can fund a resource benefit. Preserve those flags through every descendant. Capacity changes are not damage or healing. Ordinary healing observes actual blockers, modifiers, finite reserves and the Critical ceiling; direct state recovery is identified separately and remains subject to broad HP-gain prohibition. A successful stabilization or life-state change does not silently remove Wounds, Prone or another unconsciousness cause.
NEW common anti-loop binding for the new feat rewards: preserve original actor, paid event and target; no staged cooperative threat, vanished/no-resource body, copied packet, reflected retaliation, cost damage or manufactured repeat kill supplies another free resource, attack, healing conversion or reset. Explicit independent printed exceptions are listed in the relevant row, not inferred by name. A root's refunded RP cannot exceed the real unrefunded payment eligible for that particular refund, and headroom still caps restoration. One refund record cannot be spent twice by Arcane Resonance and Arcane Recall. A new feat supplies no RP pool. Reactions require actual availability; specifically passive post-zero registration/recovery exceptions do not grant an Action or Reaction at zero HP. Automatic death processing still precedes later generic regeneration unless the exact source supplies the narrow earlier recovery window.

## Field Medic — General; trained in Medicine

As a Bonus Action, use one actual healer's-kit use on one legally reachable living dying creature. Resolve the canonical automatic kit stabilization, including its normal1d4-hour recovery deadline. Inventory must contain a real remaining use; this feat invents no kit capacity. This is distinct from the ordinary Action/DC10 Wisdom(Medicine) stabilization option.

Whenever you actually cause a dying→Stable transition by **any legal method**, offer the target your PB temporary HP with default lifetime. Record the transition when it occurs. Already-Stable creatures cannot be stabilized again for a new grant. Record one entitlement per target + actual dying episode + feat owner, plus the actual stabilization event ID. Different owners do not share an artificial family lock, but each must actually cause a valid transition. A new episode requires a genuine exit from the old dying episode and later entry into dying; damage absorbed entirely by temporary HP does not create one.

If you also possess Battlefield Medic's separately sourced Trauma Response, first record the actual kit stabilization, then resolve that background's independent1HP recovery, then resolve Field Medic's temporary-HP offer. The later1HP does not erase the stabilization trigger. The feat itself provides no normal HP, consciousness, Wound removal or resurrection. No background is granted by acquiring this feat.

**NEW integration:** event/episode anti-replay identity and ordering with independent recovery; the broad “when you stabilize” trigger is preserved.

completeUnchangedReviewedRecord.operationalRules:
## Lifeleech — Magic; actual spellcasting ability

Before your spell's damage resolves, designate one eligible hostile target for that spell root and canonical round/window. Your first positive actual necrotic damage to that target in the window commits the entitlement, even if the eventual healing is0, prohibited, capped or unfunded. No retargeting after observing results; area spells do not harvest a separate heal from every target. The same continuing spell can qualify again in a later real round/window.

Raw self-healing is `floor(actual necrotic damage dealt /2)`. Use only the actual necrotic component, including actual temporary-HP absorption and normal HP lost under the existing actual-damage interface; no overkill. Targets must be genuine hostile opposition, not friendly/staged/trivial sacrifices or owner/ally-generated farming bodies. Natural attacks, Agony Lance and the Necrotic Affinity die alone are not spells. The feat removes no Wounds and cannot resurrect its dead owner.

**NEW finite resource — Lifeleech Recovery Reserve:** newly acquiring the feat starts at0. At each actual completed long rest set its capacity and remaining points to `2 × current character level`, snapshotted then. Level/PB changes between rests do not refill/recompute it. This reserve is neither RP nor Mutation Recovery Reserve. Persistent save imports must preserve validated spent state.

Run the ordinary two-pass healing modifiers/reductions/prohibitions. Preview uses available reserve to determine whether conditional bonuses requiring positive actual HP restoration qualify. Apply reductions before funding. Cap final legal healing potential by remaining reserve; spend that **entire funded amount** on commitment, including funded excess. All lawful healing bonuses consume this same reserve. Then restore HP subject to ordinary maximum HP and Critical ceiling, and calculate `genuine excess = max(0, funded amount − ordinary missing HP)`.

A broad HP-gain prohibition produces0 legal amount, spends0 reserve and creates0 excess. At reserve0 the round/root trigger still commits, but it produces neither restoration nor excess. Full HP can produce funded excess, but does not enable conditional bonuses requiring actual HP restoration. Critical's ceiling does not itself turn all unrestored points into excess.

Lifeleech provides no intrinsic excess converter. A separately authorized converter must have its own eligibility/cost/cadence/cap and consume each funded excess point once. An explicitly legal resource-output converter remains possible; incidental heal-triggered resource production is blocked. The child heal carries `noLifeleechRetrigger`, `blockHealCopyTriggers` and `blockResourceTriggers`; propagate these to downstream callers. The resource flag blocks incidental triggers, not an exact, separately paid excess-conversion transaction. No new resource converter is granted here.

Lifeleech also automatically collects one Soul Charge at an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, perceived with legal line of effect. No crystal is required for Lifeleech's own collection. Use the shared resource/death rules below. Lifeleech alone cannot spend charges through abilities from the unowned Soul Cage feat.

## Necrotic Affinity — Magic; Religion proficiency **or** character level8+

You have resistance to necrotic damage. Once per actual turn, when you hit with a melee attack, you may add1d6 necrotic damage. Natural/form melee attacks and off-turn Reaction attacks can qualify. A critical hit doubles this die to2d6; extra Actions in the same turn do not refresh it, while a genuinely different extra turn has its own entitlement. The die is feat damage, not spell damage.

Preserve the previously reviewed absorption procedure: when a legal necrotic spell/supernatural packet reaches the post-passive-defense stage, you may pay your Reaction to prevent `floor(post-defense necrotic damage /2)` before the old temporary-HP buffer. Resolve the remaining canonical damage once. Afterwards, if the holder remains living, offer temporary HP equal to the prevented amount until the end of the holder's next original regular turn, using its real endpoint marker. A1-point packet spends the Reaction but prevents/grants0. New temporary HP cannot absorb that same packet. Use `BufferLedger.necrotic_affinity` and `finish_necrotic_affinity`; do not apply resistance or damage twice.

When a creature actually dies from a canonical fatal damage/death root containing positive qualifying necrotic harm **owned by you**, attach a Necrotic Affinity seal to that death instance for24 elapsed hours. This includes your spells, the feat die, Agony Lance or another genuinely personal necrotic source. It is not limited to the feat's1d6. Supplying a summoned/transformed creature's statistics does not make its damage yours.

A mixed-type fatal root qualifies if your positive resolved necrotic component belongs to that root and the root actually causes death; no counterfactual subtraction test. Direct Instant Death, fatal death failures at0HP, or a later consequence expressly preserving that necrotic causal root can qualify. Temporary-HP-only absorption with no harmful consequence does not establish a seal.

The seal blocks applicable resurrection with an **actual spellRank/effectiveRank0..5**. Never invent a rank for unranked class features. Reviewed Paladin Grace Reversal is rank5 and is blocked; ordinary Resurrection7 and True Resurrection9 are above this restriction. Other resurrection requirements and Soul Bind still apply independently.

Same owner/death instance does not duplicate; different owners can have separate endpoints, but boolean blocking does not compound. A seal ends by elapsed expiry or an exact source able to remove that blocker, not generic cure. A legal return to life closes that death instance; its historical seals do not persist onto a later death. Transformations never create a new soul/body identity to evade a seal.

**NEW integration:** actual-turn identity, rank translation and fatal-root/death-instance bookkeeping. The broader printed necrotic-kill scope is preserved, correcting the narrower first draft.

anatomy_lore.name: Anatomy Lore

sourceObject.name: Anatomy Lore
sourceObject.description: You have studied the weak joints, organs, and pressure points of giants, ogres, and other colossal foes common to Aethel's wilds. Prestige lineage: Giant Killer. completed from the existing development record.)
sourceObject.prerequisite: Intelligence 13+, proficiency in Knowledge (Monstrous Humanoids) or Survival
sourceObject.effect: As a bonus action, you can identify one weak point on a Large or larger creature you can see. Your next attack against that creature deals +50% damage if it hits, or you gain advantage on the attack if the target is Huge or larger. Once per short rest, when you hit a colossal foe with this advantage, you may force it to succeed on a Strength save or have its speed halved until the end of your next turn.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: As a Bonus Action, mark one actually visible Large-or-larger creature with a perceivable physical weak point and legal line of effect. NEW: maximum range 60 feet; keep at most one such mark, replacing the old one without refund. At marking choose damage mode, or advantage mode if the target is Huge or larger. The mark lasts until the end of your next original regular turn, using the current virtual-marker rules if initiative changes. It is consumed by your next actual attack roll against that target, hit or miss; attacks against others neither consume it nor receive its benefit. Damage mode adds half, rounded down, of that attack's own rolled weapon/natural/unarmed damage dice plus its ordinary ability modifier after its actual critical-dice adjustment, minimum zero. Do not include spell damage, separate riders, copied damage, added Smite/sneak dice or another percentage enhancement in this proposal's base. Add this extra amount as the attack's native damage type before target defenses, once. Advantage mode gives advantage to that next attack; ordinary cancellation still applies. Once per completed short rest, after an actual hit from advantage mode against a Huge-or-larger marked target, you may spend the use to force a Strength save against DC 8 + PB + INT modifier. On failure halve that target's current applicable movement Speeds until the end of your next original regular turn; do not stack same-family halves. NEW: the rider can qualify when the feat's advantage was canceled, because the selected paid mode still applied. The creature must possess relevant anatomy; no taxonomy or immunity is rewritten. The same attack cannot claim this proposed percentage enhancement and another percentage enhancement on the same base: select one, retaining other independently legal flat/dice riders.
sourceDirection.submittedNewChoices: Range, mark deadline/consumption, actual anatomical gate, damage base and ordering, mode lock, DC, Huge meaning of colossal, canceled-advantage bridge and percentage-family rule. Must confer with Precision Strike/Giant Slayer and full class damage scope.
submittedWorkedCases: A legal marked damage-mode weapon hit has 2d6 totaling 7 plus STR 3: its base is 10 and the rider adds 5 before defenses. An independent 1d6 damage rider is resolved normally but is not included in that half-base.

Against a Huge foe, choose advantage mode. If disadvantage cancels it and the ordinary roll still hits, the proposed slow rider may spend its short-rest use; a successful Strength save prevents the slow but does not refund that use.
sourceDirection.decision: Preserve source next-attack scope including spell attacks, remove invented weapon-only exclusion and percentage monopoly; retain real anatomy, one mark, Huge choice and the paid slow.

sourceObject.effect: You can use a healer's kit to restore hit points and stabilize dying creatures more effectively.

healer.originalQuestion: The source has no HP amount, action, target cadence or kit-charge cost. Complete all of them, including stabilization versus actual healing, touch/access and zeroHP/Wound gates. Bind the actual ten-charge Healer kit and compare the already-reviewed Field Medic plus pending Field Surgeon, without double expenditure, invented charges or unbounded repeat healing.

sourceDirection.name: Healer
sourceDirection.originalQuestion: The source has no HP amount, action, target cadence or kit-charge cost. Complete all of them, including stabilization versus actual healing, touch/access and zeroHP/Wound gates. Bind the actual ten-charge Healer kit and compare the already-reviewed Field Medic plus pending Field Surgeon, without double expenditure, invented charges or unbounded repeat healing.

originalSourceObject.name: Healer
originalSourceObject.description: You are skilled in medicine and healing.
originalSourceObject.effect: You can use a healer's kit to restore hit points and stabilize dying creatures more effectively.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: NEW full healing procedure: as an Action, spend one real healer's-kit charge to treat one adjacent legally reachable living creature. Choose ordinary stabilization only, or this feat's healing treatment. A full actual kit has ten charges, costs 5 gp and weighs 3 lb under the reviewed item rule; transfer or partial use never refills it. Healing treatment has one entitlement per recipient per that recipient's completed short or long rest, shared across all Healer practitioners. Commit that entitlement and the charge before resolution even if healing is later blocked. If the recipient is dying, first cause an actual dying-to-Stable transition using this paid kit use, then resolve ordinary healing of 2d4 plus the practitioner's signed Wisdom modifier, minimum zero before the normal healing pipeline. One charge funds both parts of this single treatment. If HP gain is blocked, the stabilization remains with its genuine recovery deadline; if positive HP returns, close that obsolete deadline normally. A recipient whose healing entitlement is spent may still receive ordinary kit stabilization for its real charge and Action, without more feat HP. Already Stable creatures can receive the once-per-rest healing but create no new stabilization trigger. This removes no Wounds, Injury, disease or death. Independently owned Field Medic/Field Surgeon triggers require their actual source/event and own limits, with no duplicated kit charge or invented second stabilization.
sourceDirection.submittedNewChoices: Action, one-charge cost, 2d4+WIS healing, recipient short-rest family cap, blocked-offer commitment and stabilization-before-healing sequence.
submittedWorkedCases: One charge treats a dying target: record stabilization, then dice 3+2 and WIS +3 give 8 ordinary healing before actual modifiers/caps. A second Healer owner cannot repeat the HP treatment before that target rests.
Under a broad HP-gain prohibition the target remains Stable at zero; the charge and healing entitlement are spent. The feat does not resurrect a dead body.

sourceObject.description: Practiced recall recovers a spent spell through a deliberate return to its familiar pattern.
sourceObject.effect: After casting a ranked spell, recover RP equal to that spell’s tier, to a maximum of 5 RP. You regain this use after a long rest.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Regain used spell once per day
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: After a completed personal rank 1–9 cast, optionally consume the once LR use to recover min(actual rank,5, RP headroom, unrefunded RP actually paid for that cast). NEW the funding ceiling counts only actual personal RP expenditure, including legal surcharges; it cannot refund charges, HP, other pools, free price or an ally’s contribution. Register the cast’s paid RP and every direct refund/recovery against the same expense once, across this feat and other refund sources; choose a legal order without exceeding that expense. A legal fully saved/missed cast qualifies; countered/interrupted, copied or released-again casts do not. A readied cast qualifies once when successfully prepared, never at release. If the computed recovery is 0, decline before committing the use; no newRPpool/cap. Ordinary ongoing effects need not finish their entire duration.

elvenAccuracy.name: Elven Accuracy

sourceObject.name: Elven Accuracy
sourceObject.description: Your elven heritage grants supernatural accuracy.
sourceObject.effect: When you have advantage on an attack roll using Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can reroll one of the dice.

elvenAccuracy.originalQuestion: Preserve Elf or half-elf eligibility without inventing an absent half-elf ancestry alias. For an advantaged DEX/INT/WIS/CHA attack define optional reroll of one die, timing, must-use-new result, number of rerolls and advantage cancellation. No automatic third die on disadvantage, STR attacks or repeated same-die chains.

For an advantaged DEX/INT/WIS/CHA attack define optional reroll of one die, timing, must-use-new result, number of rerolls and advantage cancellation. No automatic third die on disadvantage, STR attacks or repeated same-die chains.

originalSourceObject.name: Elven Accuracy
originalSourceObject.description: Your elven heritage grants supernatural accuracy.
originalSourceObject.effect: When you have advantage on an attack roll using Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can reroll one of the dice.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Require an actual Elf ancestry receipt or a genuine independently sourced half-elf receipt; do not create or alias an absent half-elf base. On an attack actually made with advantage usingDEX,INT,WIS orCHA, after seeing the two original d20s and before final hit/outcome declaration, you may reroll one chosen die once and must use its new face in that position. Then keep the higher of the two resulting dice. NEW at most one Elven Accuracy reroll per attack; it cannot reroll the same die again through this feature or create a third independent kept die. If any disadvantage cancels advantage, there is one ordinary die and this feature is ineligible. STR/CON attacks, saves and checks do not qualify. Keep actual natural-face provenance for criticals. Lucky's separate die replacement may affect this attack only under its own one-event procedure; no Elven reroll of that additional Lucky die.
sourceDirection.submittedNewChoices: Actual ancestry receipt, replace-one-die procedure, before-outcome timing and no reroll loop.
submittedWorkedCases: An advantagedDEX attack rolls4 and12. Reroll4 to9, then keep12; rerolling does not guarantee improvement.
Advantage canceled by disadvantage yields one d20, so Elven Accuracy cannot trigger.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: NEW gain3luck points, initially full and restored to3 only on a completedLR; no overcap or conversion. On your own attack, ability/skill/tool check or save, after the initial d20 die/dice are visible but before the outcome and consequences are declared, spend at most1point to roll one additionald20. Choose either to keep the original dice unchanged or to replace one original die with the new face; then apply the roll's original normal/advantage/disadvantage selection over its original one/two positions. The added die is not a third freely best-kept die under disadvantage. Actual natural face is the final kept face; no source allows inventing an automatic result. It may affect an opposed check or death save because those are your checks/saves; it cannot reroll an enemy, a damage die, a flat result or a no-roll automatic failure. NEW one Lucky intervention per underlying roll event even if another rule later rerolls it. Resolve Elven Accuracy on initial eligible dice first, then Lucky; Elven Accuracy cannot reroll the added Lucky die. Other mandatory whole-roll replacements preserve their own order and consume the same event entitlement.

sourceDirection.submittedProcedure: Add 2 on actual Constitution saving throws whose purpose is maintaining concentration on a real active effect. This does not create concentration on an effect that lacks it, grant a new slot or add to every Constitution save. Separately add 1 on actual Wisdom saves against a mental effect under the shared proposed finite predicate. The two clauses have different roll requirements and do not both apply to one ordinary Constitution concentration save. Preserve the current source's save wording over its legacy 'concentration checks' shorthand; an effect using a different non-save procedure is not automatically converted. NEW: its distinct qualifying Wisdom +1 can coexist with Iron Will's +2 under the proposed feat-family rule. No effect without an actual save grants an invented roll, and no bonus automatically prevents concentration ending from Incapacitated, voluntary replacement or its source's dependency ending.

A qualifying WIS save against mental coercion can receive the +1, while an unrelated Wisdom-based navigation check receives nothing.

fullSharedRules.title: Distinct feat bonuses and retained comparison families
fullSharedRules.wording:
NEW joint convention: after eligibility, flat numeric bonuses from DISTINCT feat identities add unless an explicit shared comparison family says otherwise. One feat identity contributes once to the same event/statistic across duplicate representations, sources and owners. This replaces Extended Magic's blanket strongest-same-stat proposal and the conflicting individual statements/examples named in the correction register. It does not rewrite the eight reviewed feats or reviewed maximum-HP components.
Class techniques still perform their own strongest-class-bonus comparison; spells perform their reviewed same-stat comparison; item, attire, tool, facility, cover and item-enhancement contributions retain their own reviewed families. Then add the independently legal feat contribution. A feat-created weapon/armor enhancement explicitly put into an equipment family remains there, not also a feat bonus. Same named condition penalties retain their own comparison rather than becoming additive because a feat created them. Advantage/disadvantage still cancel normally; more sources of advantage do not outvote one disadvantage. Damage resistance of the same scope applies once; immunity retains priority; keep the greatest remaining temporary HP, not their sum. Expanded critical ranges use the broadest applicable range rather than adding chance points. Copies cannot exploit a new family name to duplicate a source. Actual unusual source overrides retain their explicitly narrower predicates.

fullSharedRules.title: Native damage, percentages and hostile slows
fullSharedRules.wording:
NEW percentage convention: each separately eligible percentage feat computes its own floored increment from the SAME native packet, after actual critical-dice adjustment and its ordinary native ability/flat formula but BEFORE external riders, other percentage increments, saves and defenses. Add the increments; never multiply them together or floor a combined percentage instead of the separate increments. A feat's exact eligible base remains controlling: Anatomy Lore and Precision Strike do not acquire a giant-slayer multiplier on unrelated spells, for example. Added external Smite/sneak/copy/retaliation/rider packets do not enter another feat's native base unless expressly named. Apply a shared-area roll's increment once to that shared roll, then each actual target's save/defenses. For a mixed native packet requiring division, compute the increment once, distribute proportional to nonnegative native typed amounts by largest remainder with original component order breaking ties, and preserve integer totals. Do not add the full increment to each type. Additional dice are added before actual critical doubling and save fractions; a maximized die is not an actually rolled face for rolled-face triggers.
KEEP hostile slow arbitration: evaluate each adverse Speed effect against the same pre-control Speed and take the lowest surviving result; do not add Slasher and Crippling Strike's two -10 penalties, or subtract -10 again after a stronger half-Speed. Distinct records retain their own deadlines and suppression. Root/physical restraint, missing movement modes, terrain costs, burden, systemic Strain and actual Wounds retain their proper independent stages. No movement already spent is refunded. Percent damage addition is not the rule for percentage work/cost/consumption reductions: those use their specifically declared strongest-factor family.

fullSharedRules.title: Roll type, reroll window and targets
fullSharedRules.wording:
KEEP attacks versus AC, binary saves, fixed-DC Core tasks with natural shifts, and opposed totals with unchanged-state ties lost by the initiator. A +10 attack margin is not a critical. Natural 1/20 on attacks retain their attack rules; saves do not acquire task shifts. A failed-save reroll replaces the whole original one- or two-d20 procedure with the same actual modifiers and advantage/disadvantage, before consequences, unless the exact feat instead replaces a named die position. Use the replacement even if worse; a source cannot reroll its own replacement. Lucky and Elven Accuracy keep their separately specified die-position rules. Costs and prior consequences are not rolled back.
KEEP the current class target convention: 'ally' includes the owner unless the source says OTHER, or real geometry/activity inherently requires a different creature. Do not count the same person twice in 'you and an ally', a team, a flanking pair or an assistance role. 'Enemy' requires an actual current opponent, not every creature in range; meaningful-hostility and anti-farm gates apply only where the source/this register binds resource or encounter rewards. Do not add an enemy or anatomy gate to an unrelated ordinary attack merely as a blanket convention. Source perception, actual reach/line of effect, body eligibility and willing/understood channels remain real.

fullSharedRules.title: One clock, deadlines, rests and initial uses
fullSharedRules.wording:
Use EX58's single elapsed clock, eight-hour Watches, actual task minutes, two-active-work-Watch ceiling and scheduled Rest. A change of scene, gate, holder, location, initiative, class representation or calendar label does not reset a resource. SR/LR in these new procedures mean the actual beneficial completed owner rest, with one beneficial Long Rest per 24 elapsed hours and at most two beneficial Short Rests between beneficial Long Rests. A qualifying long rest restores a short-rest allowance as already governed. Extra safe Rest paying Rest Debt alone provides no second resource recovery. Recipient-rest limits use the actual named recipient's rest epoch.
NEW initial acquisition completion: the newly acquired limited-use feat begins with its specified full finite allowance, unless it expressly starts empty (such as accumulated stacks/charges). Reacquisition/alias duplication cannot initialize it again. An increase in a PB-based maximum increases capacity only, not current unspent uses. Genuine maximum-HP/RP/RC, Hit Die, reserve and slot changes never heal or refill unrelated current values.
Use each explicit own-turn/any-turn/round predicate literally. A per-round allowance has one numbered global-round identity; extra turns do not refresh it. A default 'your turn' feat allowance uses the owner's regular interval unless its exact source direction expressly retains any actual turn. Newly completed missing durations use the next future original regular marker specified by the row, not the already-underway marker, retaining virtual/absolute deadlines across schedule changes. Outside initiative use the governed six-second phase without double ticks. A missed trigger is not queued for later. An early ending does not refund time or a use.

NEW FEAT335-CADENCE-CHECK-01 completion, limited to feat procedures governed by FS-06: an otherwise unqualified "once per turn" allowance is once for that feat owner during each genuine actual creature turn in which its exact trigger legally occurs, whether that turn belongs to the owner or another creature. A separately sourced and actually occurring extra turn has a distinct actual-turn identity and can supply a distinct opportunity for that unqualified allowance; this rule grants no extra turn. Another Action, Bonus Action, attack, Reaction, nested event, target or resumed segment of the same actual turn does not create another turn identity. Returning to or replaying an already recorded turn retains that turn's spent claim. Actual body, movement, attack, casting, payment, causal-root and recipient restrictions still govern independently.

This completion does not replace an expressly regular-turn allowance or FS-06's existing default owner-regular-interval allowance for "your turn". In particular, Savage Attacker retains its stated own/off-turn regular-turn allowances, and Eldritch Combat retains its expressly regular-creature-turn shared embedded-cast cap plus its owner-regular-interval ordinary-append cap. Overrun's per-creature challenge limit belongs to the actual turn containing its qualifying Dash and subsequent movement; another Dash in that same turn does not renew it. Quickened Thought keeps its expressly any-later-actual-turn release window and the shared one-free-stored-release-per-owner/numbered-round cap, not a new bank at each turn. fullSharedRules.title: Damage, current capacity, healing and causal budgets
fullSharedRules.wording:
Keep the reviewed damage/prevention/temp-HP/HP/Wound/death order and exact immunity/resistance/interception windows. Numeric actual damage means actual normal HP lost plus actual temporary HP absorbed, excluding overkill, damage prevented and mere state assignments. That metric never defeats an explicit no-resource origin, no-trigger ward/temp-HP rule or other causal prohibition: only source-qualified events can fund a resource benefit. Preserve those flags through every descendant. Capacity changes are not damage or healing. Ordinary healing observes actual blockers, modifiers, finite reserves and the Critical ceiling; direct state recovery is identified separately and remains subject to broad HP-gain prohibition. A successful stabilization or life-state change does not silently remove Wounds, Prone or another unconsciousness cause.
NEW common anti-loop binding for the new feat rewards: preserve original actor, paid event and target; no staged cooperative threat, vanished/no-resource body, copied packet, reflected retaliation, cost damage or manufactured repeat kill supplies another free resource, attack, healing conversion or reset. Explicit independent printed exceptions are listed in the relevant row, not inferred by name. A root's refunded RP cannot exceed the real unrefunded payment eligible for that particular refund, and headroom still caps restoration. One refund record cannot be spent twice by Arcane Resonance and Arcane Recall. A new feat supplies no RP pool. Reactions require actual availability; specifically passive post-zero registration/recovery exceptions do not grant an Action or Reaction at zero HP. Automatic death processing still precedes later generic regeneration unless the exact source supplies the narrow earlier recovery window.

sourceObject.name: Field Surgeon
sourceObject.description: A Wisdom-trained medic uses Medicine to stabilize an ally at 1 HP.
sourceObject.effect: When you successfully stabilize a dying creature with Medicine or a healer’s kit, it regains 1 hit point. A creature can benefit from this feat once per long rest.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Stabilize ally with 1 HP using Medicine
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

fullSelectedFeatRecords.originalQuestion: Bind genuine stabilization of a dying creature through Medicine or an actual kit, action/payment and successful event timing. Resolve once-per-Long-Rest per recipient versus practitioner, positive-healing gates, anti-loop ledgers and coexistence with reviewed Field Medic tempHP. Stable/already-conscious/dead subjects do not manufacture a new stabilization event.
